title: Beckmann Transport Models: From Autonomous Flows to One-Step Maps
claim: A single time-independent flow carries every starting point onto the data manifold, so the endpoint map is constant along trajectories.
layout: 1 wide panel, flow-field blob left, two equation boxes right
description: A large dashed beige oval, labeled supp(μ0), is filled with faint green streamlines that all sweep from upper left to lower right. A thick curve crosses the oval and is labeled M1 = supp(μ1). Its color shifts from red-brown on the left to green in the middle to blue on the right. Several trajectories start at dots at the top, including x0 ~ μ0 and X_t(x0), and hit the curve at points such as x1. Each trajectory takes the color of the point where it lands, which illustrates the level sets of T. Small flower photos mark points on the manifold. A noise image sits at the start of one trajectory. On the right, two beige boxes hold the ODE dX/dt = b(X_t) and the level-set identities b·∇T = 0, T|M1 = id and T(x0) = T(X_t(x0)) = x1.
caption: Overview of autonomous flow matching. Under Assumptions [ref]--[ref], the autonomous flow $\dot X_t=b(X_t)$ transports $\mu_0$-almost every initial point to $M_1$ at hitting time $\tau$, defining the transport map $T=X_{\tau}$ that pushes $\mu_0$ forward to $\mu_1$. The endpoint construction selects $T$; its constancy along trajectories, $(d/dt)T(X_t)=0$, implies the conservation equation $b\cdot\nabla T=0$ and motivates a direct learning objective.
abstract: We propose an instantiation of flow matching that relies on a time-independent velocity field---an autonomous flow---to exactly map between two distributions when the target is supported on a sufficiently lower-dimensional data manifold. We also show that the associated one-step generative map is constant in the direction of the autonomous velocity field and therefore satisfies a simple conservation equation, which motivates learning the map directly from samples. These autonomous flows and maps give a dynamical meaning to the flux constraint of Beckmann's transportation problem, and we show that, under suitable conditions, the construction extends beyond flow matching to other probability fluxes satisfying the same constraint. The resulting framework includes, for instance, a closed-form Coulomb transport closely related to Poisson Flow and a flow-matching-consistent version of Equilibrium Matching. We illustrate these distinctions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the autonomous flow and the one-step map on ImageNet $256\times256$.
